transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name], one of the psychiatrists here. To start, can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?

Um, yeah. I guess what finally scared me into coming in is work stuff. I’m a camera operator and editor, and I keep making these really dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make.

Like I’ll label camera cards wrong, or miss a timecode note, or export a client cut and somehow the wrong lower-third is still in there, even after I’ve checked it. And then I’ll think, “How did I not catch that?” It’s embarrassing, because it’s basic stuff. I’ve been doing this long enough that it shouldn’t be happening.

Sorry, I’m probably jumping around — it’s just been making me really nervous, like I can’t trust myself with details I used to feel solid about.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of mistakes and attention lapses — has this been a lifelong pattern for you, or did it start more recently, like in the past few weeks or months?

It’s not like it just started a few weeks ago. The really disruptive level has been… about two years, maybe two years and a couple months.

It kind of lines up with when the company did this readjustment and the way my shoots and edit reviews changed. Before that I mean, I was never perfect, nobody is, and production is always chaos — like you’re juggling batteries and cards and someone’s asking about lunch at the same time — but since that change, the mistakes started feeling much more obvious and harder to brush off.
Over these past two years, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and enjoyment in things you used to like, even outside of work?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a big, constant way. I mean, I get upset after I mess something up, obviously, and then I’ll kind of spiral about it for the day, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad all the time.

And I still like things, I think. Like if I actually sit down to watch something good or I’m on a shoot that’s going well, I can enjoy it. Although lately I feel like even watching stuff, I end up noticing continuity errors or thinking about how they lit a scene, and then I’m not really relaxing — sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed losing interest across the board outside of work. Mostly it’s the work mistakes making me feel stressed.

Thinking back to childhood and school, did you have similar problems with attention, forgetfulness, or careless mistakes back then, or is this pattern something that only really showed up in adulthood?

Yeah, I mean… looking back, there was definitely stuff when I was a kid. I didn’t think of it as “attention problems” at the time, because I was just, you know, the kid who couldn’t stay put.

In elementary school teachers moved my desk more than once because I’d be out of my seat, or blurting out answers before they finished asking, or bugging the person next to me without really meaning to. I remember being surprised people were annoyed, like I hadn’t even realized I was doing it.

Sorry, I’m thinking about this one classroom where they put my desk right by the teacher’s desk, which felt like being on display all day. So… yeah, it wasn’t only adulthood. Some version of it was there pretty early.

Aside from worrying about work mistakes, do you find yourself excessively worrying about a lot of different things in your life — like health, finances, relationships, or other everyday matters — even when there's no clear reason to?

Not really… I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess. Like if a bill is due or if someone texts “we need to talk,” my brain goes, okay, great, what happened. But I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about everything all the time for no reason.

It’s mostly when something at work goes wrong, then I can’t let it go. But health, money, relationships… not in that constant way, no. At least I don’t think so.
